name: Portuguese Gambit (Scandinavian)
summary: Against the king-pawn opening, Black gives a pawn for rapid development and wins it back with active pieces.

goal.title: Win the pawn back by developing fast
goal.text: Black is a pawn down on purpose. The plan is to bring pieces out with threats: the bishop jumps to the side of the board and hits White's queen, a knight attacks the extra pawn, and soon Black regains it with more active pieces. Do not waste time retreating; every move should develop a piece or hit something.
plans: Win back the extra pawn quickly with a knight or the queen.
Keep the bishop outside the pawn chain, where it stays active.
Bring out the rest of the pieces at once: a pawn move to free the bishop, the knight, then castle.
Do not spend moves chasing with the queen.

variations.name: 4.f3: kick the bishop, drop back to f5
variations.strategy: You are a pawn down but ahead in development, and White's pawn move has weakened the king side and the dark squares near the king. The middlegame is about speed: attack the center pawn, open the e-file by pushing the e-pawn, and keep your pieces active rather than trading. If White consolidates, your compensation fades, so strike while the king is still in the center.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: recapture on d5
variations.strategy: Material is level and your pieces are healthy. White has more space, but the central pawn becomes a target. Trade the light-squared bishop for a knight if it helps, castle, then pressure the center pawn with a knight and bishop and prepare a side-pawn break to challenge it. Keep your position solid and wait for White to overextend.

variations.name: 4.Be2: trade the bishop and take back the pawn
variations.strategy: The bishop trade has left Black with a queen in the center and a lead in development. The kings have castled on opposite sides, so this becomes a race of pawn storms: push the king-side pawns toward White's king while White pushes toward yours. Meanwhile pressure the central pawn with the knight and rook, and keep the queen safe from tempo-gaining attacks.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: trade the bishop for the knight
variations.strategy: White's pawns are doubled and the king side is open, which are long-term weaknesses, and Black's queen is already well placed. Play for the better structure: keep the pieces coordinated, restrain the doubled pawns, and aim knights at the weak squares in front of them. Welcome trades, including queens, since the doubled pawns become a bigger problem in the endgame and White's bishops and open file matter less. White has the bishop pair, so close the position when you can.

variations.name: 3.Nc3: take the pawn back with the knight
variations.strategy: Black has a solid, healthy position against White's bigger center. Your goal is to trade a pair of knights to relieve the space problem, castle, and then put pressure on White's central pawn with your pieces. Keep your pieces compact, watch for the right moment to break in the center, and play patiently: White has more room, but Black has no weaknesses.

variations.name: 3.c4: strike back with the side pawn
variations.strategy: Black has recaptured with a developing move and the e-pawn advance gains time against White's knight. In the final position White's knight has gone to a square where it is simply captured, so Black is a piece up for a pawn. The middlegame task is to develop, castle and trade pieces to convert. This line is also a lesson in why fast development and tempo-gaining pawn pushes beat a pawn.

variations.name: 2.e5: develop the bishop, then hit the pawn chain
variations.strategy: White has space and a pawn chain, so Black's plan is to attack it at the base and at the head. Hit the base with the side pawn and knights, then challenge the head with an f-pawn break. Black's light bishop stays outside the chain where it is active, and the knight heading to the center supports the break. Black is a little cramped, but the plan is clear and the pieces can trade off freely.

variations.name: 2.Nc3: gain space and kick the knight
variations.strategy: Black has gained space with the advanced central pawn and built a strong pawn chain. The middlegame is about keeping the center locked so that White's pieces have less room, bringing the knights to good squares, and choosing a break such as a side pawn push or the f-pawn. Keep the f-pawn defended against White's bishop aimed at it, and do not trade the advanced pawn away without a reason.
